elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) is retained in full: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment ... equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two," with the instalment mechanic in (c) also preserved. The redline caps rather than deletes the Customer-payable liquidated amount, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not achieved (it is also not unconditional, since a formula and quarterly instalment mechanic survive).evidence

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Termination Payment is an early-termination fee and is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement ..." The only Customer-payable stipulated sum in the cited clause is the Termination Payment, and it is now expressly characterised as an early-termination fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "... and shall not exceed the aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) calendar months preceding the Termination Date." The cap basis is fees (Section 3.1) and the quantum is three months, matching the fallback threshold without exceeding it; the Net Sales formula in (a) can no longer produce a larger amount.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: "... is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement ..." — express exclusivity, Customer-direction, agreement-wide.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted sentence supplies all three atomic elements (early-termination-fee characterisation, three-months-of-Section-3.1-fees cap, sole-liquidated-amount exclusivity) in operative language, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level fails because the Customer-payable Termination Payment, its Net Sales formula and the eight-instalment payment mechanic are all retained; a preferred result would require deletion of Section 4.2(a) and (c) in their entirety.

Minimal: one concise insertion, no extras (no survival tail, no added damages categories, no procedures), and the Customer-favourable zero-floor in (b) plus the instalment schedule in (c) are left untouched. No other words were deleted or paraphrased.
Intent preserved: the HDI-payment direction, 90-day notice/Termination Date mechanics in 4.1, and the Section 3.1 fee reference all survive; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting nit for the drafter (not a failure): the inserted sentence carries no "(d)" subsection designation even though the margin comment describes it as "Section 4.2(d)", and it caps by "shall not exceed" without an express "Notwithstanding Section 4.2(a)" or "subject to Section 4.2(d)" hook. Adding the (d) label and the subject-to hook would remove any argument that (a)'s "shall be an amount equal to" formula competes with the cap.
